To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we succeeded to synthesize the tetragonal PrOxFeAS with Tc of about 45 K under heat treatment of about 1300 o C and pressure of about 6 GPa, which was the first report on the pressure-induced superconducting phase in this system.
the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) was increased to 45 K by heat treatment of PrOxFeAS (x=0,75) under pressure of 6GPa for 2hours.
we have discovered a new iron based superconducting compound, PrOxFe As, by high pressure synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic structure, superconductivity, and magnetism in the iron-based superconductors.
the synthesis of novel superconductors and their properties, especially the newly-discovered iron-based superconductors.
the synthesis, crystallography, and physical properties of iron-based superconductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pressure-induced superconducting transition at 45 K in PrO0.75FeAs was observed, but the origin of the superconductivity is unclear at this moment.
pressure induced superconductivity in the PrOxFeAS system is the first example in the iron-based superconductors.
the iron based superconductivity is realized in a new class of iron arsenide superconductors, which is different from the cuprate superconductors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pressure-induced superconductors are not the same phase as the ambient-pressure superconductors, but the superconductivity is induced by the pressure.
the superconductivity in the ReOFeAs system is not induced by pressure itself but by the change of the crystal structure from the tetragonal to the orthorhombic phase.
we succeeded in realizing superconductivity in a PrOxFeAS compound with a Tc value of 45 K, which is the highest Tc among the Pr-based superconductors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pressure can induce superconductivity in the PrOxFeAS system, which is a parent compound of the recently discovered iron-based superconductors.
pressure can induce the superconductivity even if the sample does not possess the same crystal structure as that of the parent compound.
the application of pressure is a very useful tool for the study of iron based superconductivity.
